caption: With R = I and t = 0, the point (1.0, 0.5, 2.0) m is already in camera coordinates. Dividing by Z = 2.0 m gives (0.5, 0.25), multiplying by 800 px gives offsets 400 px and 200 px, and adding (320, 240) px lands at pixel (720, 440).

spec.title: Worked example: 3D point to pixel
spec.aria: A downward flow chart of the worked example: a world point with R identity and t zero becomes camera point (1.0, 0.5, 2.0) metres, is divided by Z = 2.0 metres to (0.5, 0.25), multiplied by 800 to offsets 400 and 200 pixels, added to principal point (320, 240) pixels, giving pixel (720, 440).
